title: Describing Motion
intro: Distance, speed, velocity and acceleration measured on the school field and graphed by hand.

lessons.title: What Is Motion? Position and Reference Points
lessons.focus: Motion is change of position relative to a reference; 'moving compared to what?' game; frame of reference.
lessons.advanced: Passenger in a moving matatu: at rest or in motion? Explain using reference frames.

lessons.title: Distance vs Displacement
lessons.focus: Walk an L-shaped path; distance paced vs straight-line displacement; scalar vs vector introduced.
lessons.advanced: You walk 30 m east then 40 m north: compute distance and displacement; explain why displacement can be zero after a long walk.

lessons.title: Speed: How Fast Is Fast?
lessons.focus: v = d/t; time a 40 m walk and run; compute speeds; compare class results on a chart.
lessons.advanced: A runner covers 100 m in 14.0 s: compute average speed in m/s and km/h.

lessons.title: Units of Speed: m/s Meets km/h
lessons.focus: Conversion practice; reading boda speedometer; estimating matatu speed between kilometre markers.
lessons.advanced: Show 10 m/s = 36 km/h by chain conversion; which unit suits walking, which suits highways?

lessons.title: Average vs Instantaneous Speed
lessons.focus: Market journey with stops: total distance over total time vs reading at one instant; when each matters.
lessons.advanced: A journey: 2 km in 20 min, rest 10 min, 2 km in 30 min. Compute overall average speed and explain the rest's effect.

lessons.title: Velocity: Speed with a Direction
lessons.focus: Around-the-track walks; same speed, changing velocity in a circle; vectors drawn as arrows.
lessons.advanced: Two bodas at 40 km/h, one north one east: same speed, same velocity? Draw the velocity vectors.

lessons.title: Acceleration: Changing Speed
lessons.focus: Speeding up, slowing down, turning — all acceleration; boda leaving a stage; a = Δv/t introduced.
lessons.advanced: A matatu goes 0 to 15 m/s in 10 s: compute acceleration; what force ratio a=F/m does that imply per tonne?

lessons.title: Measuring Human Speed: The 20-Metre Dash
lessons.focus: Time classmates over 20 m; chart distribution; reaction error at the stopwatch; repeatable method.
lessons.advanced: Stopwatch operator has 0.2 s reaction on start and stop: estimate the speed error for a 3.5 s dash.

lessons.title: Distance–Time Graphs I: Plotting a Steady Walk
lessons.focus: Measure positions every 5 s on a marked course; plot; straight line for steady speed.
lessons.advanced: Extract speed from your graph gradient; compare with d/t from raw numbers — why agree?

lessons.title: Distance–Time Graphs II: Stops, Speed-ups and Returns
lessons.focus: Interpret stories from graph shapes; draw graph for a boda journey with a puncture stop; match graph to story cards.
lessons.advanced: Sketch the d–t graph for a ball thrown up and caught (distance from ground vs time) and defend the shape.

lessons.title: Speed–Time Graphs
lessons.focus: Gradient = acceleration; flat = steady; area under = distance (counting squares); plot the dash data.
lessons.advanced: From a v–t graph with constant acceleration 2 m/s² for 6 s, find distance travelled by area.

lessons.title: Build: A Ticker Timer from Simple Parts
lessons.focus: Hand-pulled paper tape under a clothespin-and-rubber 'tapper' metronome; dots record motion; analyze spacing.
materials: rubber band striker or felt pen
lessons.advanced: Dot spacing grows 2→4→6 mm at 5 beats/s: compute the three speeds and the acceleration.

lessons.title: Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion
lessons.focus: Compare tape from steady pull vs falling mass pull; classify everyday motions; graph both.
lessons.advanced: Sketch d–t and v–t for uniform and for accelerating motion: four panels, labelled.

lessons.title: Motion of Vehicles: Odometers, Speedometers and Limits
lessons.focus: How speedo/odometer work (wheel rotations × circumference); why speed limits exist; NTSA context.
lessons.advanced: Wheel circumference 2.1 m turns 3 times per second: compute road speed in km/h.

lessons.title: Relative Motion: Passing and Being Passed
lessons.focus: Two walking students pass each other; speeds add/subtract; boat on flowing river stories.
lessons.advanced: Boat does 3 m/s on a river flowing 1 m/s: find effective speeds upstream and downstream and round-trip time for 600 m legs.

lessons.title: Reaction Time: The Ruler-Drop Test
lessons.focus: Catch a dropped ruler between fingers; distance fallen → reaction time via d=½gt²; chart the class.
lessons.advanced: Convert an 18 cm catch into reaction time using d=½gt² (g=10): show the working.

lessons.title: Thinking and Braking Distance
lessons.focus: Reaction distance + braking distance = stopping distance; toy-car crash demo; why tailgating kills.
lessons.advanced: At 20 m/s with 0.7 s reaction and 4 m/s² braking deceleration: compute total stopping distance.

lessons.title: Acceleration Lab: Toy Car on a Ramp
lessons.focus: Time car over measured ramp sections at different slopes; steeper → greater acceleration; graph results.
lessons.advanced: Using v²=2as with your measured time and distance, estimate acceleration on the steepest slope.

lessons.title: Rolling Down Ramps: Bottles, Balls and Cylinders
lessons.focus: Race solid ball vs bottle of water vs empty bottle; rolling is slower than sliding without friction would suggest — rotation teaser.
lessons.advanced: Explain using energy sharing between translation and rotation why the filled bottle and ball finish differently.

lessons.title: Deceleration: Slowing Down Is Acceleration Too
lessons.focus: Ball rolling out on grass; swing dying down; sign conventions for ±acceleration.
lessons.advanced: A ball enters grass at 4 m/s and stops in 2.5 m: find deceleration from v²=u²+2as.

lessons.title: Circular Motion Preview: Speed Constant, Velocity Changing
lessons.focus: Swing a stone on string; constant speed but changing direction means acceleration toward centre (deep dive Unit 10).
lessons.advanced: Argue why 'no acceleration at constant speed' fails for circular motion, using velocity vectors.

lessons.title: Project: Graph Your Journey to School
lessons.focus: Record times at landmarks on the way to school; draw d–t graph; find fastest/slowest legs; present.
lessons.advanced: Estimate uncertainty: phone-clock times ±30 s over 8 min legs — what speed uncertainty results?

lessons.title: Estimating Speed Without Instruments
lessons.focus: Calibrated pacing (your stride length), counting seconds by chant, kilometre markers; field estimates of boda speeds.
lessons.advanced: Design a zero-instrument speed survey for your road with ±20% accuracy; describe validation.

lessons.title: Motion of Animals: Cheetahs, Goats and Us
lessons.focus: Gaits and speeds; why cheetah spine flexes; ostrich vs human stride; timing a goat across the field.
lessons.advanced: Cheetah: 30 m/s for 15 s max; prey 20 m/s with 100 m head start — does the cheetah catch it? Show working.

lessons.title: Build: A Two-Gate Speed Trap for Toy Cars
lessons.focus: Two chalk gates + stopwatch (or clap-echo timing); test car designs down a ramp; class leaderboard.
lessons.advanced: Gate spacing 1.0 m, reaction error 0.15 s: which car speeds can you trust to two significant figures?

lessons.title: Unit Review: Motion Field Day
lessons.focus: Stations: dash timing, graph reading, reaction test, relative-motion demo; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Write one higher-order motion question (graph interpretation) with full marking scheme for the quiz.
